summary.en: The United States has lifted sanctions on Jorge Rodríguez, the president of Venezuela’s National Assembly, and on the head of the legislature, easing pressure on opposition leaders. The US Space Force has deployed electromagnetic weapons and electronic warfare systems against Venezuela, mirroring operations in Iran. Nicolás Maduro is returning to federal court to face torture allegations while a top economic adviser promises a debt sustainability analysis soon. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: USA har opphevet sanksjonene mot Jorge Rodríguez, presidenten i Venezuelas nasjonalforsamling, og mot lederen av lovgivende forsamling, og lettet presset på opposisjonsledere. US Space Force har satt i drift elektromagnetiske våpen og elektroniske krigssystemer mot Venezuela, i likhet med operasjoner i Iran. Nicolás Maduro vender tilbake til føderal domstol for å møte anklager om tortur mens en toppøkonomisk rådgiver lover en analyse av gjeldsbærekraft snart. To dødsfall i kamper ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
